messages.content: 你能給我從舊金山家裡到帕羅奧圖辦公室最快的路線，然後從帕羅奧圖到舊金山金門大橋的風景路線，最後從金門大橋回家最快的路線嗎？

function.name: get_directions
function.description: Retrieve directions from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_location.description: The starting point of the journey.

end_location.description: The destination point of the journey.

route_type.description: Type of route to use (e.g., fastest, scenic). Default is fastest.

message.reasoning:
The user wants directions from home in San Francisco to Palo Alto office fastest route, then from Palo Alto to Golden Gate Bridge scenic route, then from Golden Gate Bridge back home fastest route.

We need to call get_directions twice? Actually three segments: SF home -> Palo Alto office; Palo Alto -> Golden Gate Bridge; Golden Gate Bridge -> SF home.

We need to provide start_location and end_location for each. We can ask for addresses? The user didn't specify exact addresses. We might assume generic: "San Francisco home" and "Palo Alto office". But we need actual addresses or at least city names. We could interpret "San Francisco home" as "San Francisco, CA" and "Palo Alto office" as "Palo Alto, CA". For Golden Gate Bridge, we can use "Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco, CA".

Thus we will call get_directions thrice with appropriate parameters.

But the tool only allows one call per invocation. We can chain calls? We can call get_directions once with start_location "San Francisco home", end_location "Palo Alto office", route_type "fastest". Then second call with start_location "Palo Alto office", end_location "Golden Gate Bridge", route_type "scenic". Third call with start_location "Golden Gate Bridge", end_location "San Francisco home", route_type "fastest".

We need to output the results. Let's do it.
